description: Integration gate: run the inline esm-spec 6.6.5 test of problems/latlon3d_advection_3d.esm (model Advection3d, test mms_steady_3d_combined) at the problem's fixed resolution (NLON=36, NLAT=19, NLEV=10) through each binding's official simulation pathway. Exercises all THREE latlon3d directional advection rules firing together on one [lon,lat,lev] field — upwind1_D_lon_periodic + central_D_lat_zero_grad_bc + central_D_lev_zero_grad_bc — assembling into a single RHS with a forced-steady manufactured solution, to prove the rank-3 3-D advection operator composes and integrates without match conflict. The per-direction order claims are proven separately by the three latlon3d convergence cases; this manifest only routes the runners (assertions + tolerances live in the problem).

scope_excluded.go: rewrite-only port; no makearray lowering / simulator
scope_excluded.typescript: rewrite-only port; no makearray lowering / simulator

blocked_upstream_bindings.rust: Rust does not terminate on this case at any tolerance tried (Erk at the manifest's reltol 1e-10 down to a loosest reltol 1e-6 all wedge; observed >200s at 100% CPU with no output and no MaxStepsExceeded). The RHS is SMOOTH here (upwind1_D_lon_periodic + central_D_lat_zero_grad_bc + central_D_lev_zero_grad_bc — no min/max/limiter), so the trigger is problem SIZE, not non-smoothness: this is the largest simulation RHS in the suite (NLON=36 x NLAT=19 x NLEV=10 = 6840 cells with all three directional operators composed into one field). earthsci-ast-rs's diffsol integrator has no dtmin/max-step fail-fast guard, and its rejected substeps inside a single solver.step() are not counted against the outer max_steps cap (src/simulate.rs), so the adaptive controller drives dt->0 inside step() without ever returning to hit the guard. Julia (Tsit5) and Python (LSODA) both solve it (Python verified here, ok). The per-direction order claims are still fully covered on Rust by the three separate latlon3d convergence cases; only this combined 3-D integration driver is blocked. Remove once the Rust solver gains a dtmin/max-step fail-fast guard.
